text.en:
Meena cut a kite shape from paper. She folded it down the middle and the two halves matched exactly.
"Look, both sides are the same!" she said.
Her teacher smiled. "That fold line is a line of symmetry."

A shape has a line of symmetry if we can fold it along that line so that the two halves fit exactly on each other. The line is also called a line of reflection, like a mirror line.
A square has four lines of symmetry: two through the middle of opposite sides and two along the diagonals. A rectangle that is not a square has two. A circle has many, because any line through its centre works.
An equilateral triangle has three lines of symmetry. An isosceles triangle has one. A triangle with all sides different has none. Letters such as A, H and M have lines of symmetry, but F and R do not.
A shape has a line of symmetry when folding along the line makes both halves match exactly.
A square has four lines of symmetry. A rectangle has two. A circle has many.
An equilateral triangle has three lines of symmetry, an isosceles triangle has one, and a triangle with all sides different has none.
Some letters have a line of symmetry, like A, H and M. Letters like F and R do not.

problem.en: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have?

text.en: Fold the rectangle in half along its length. The halves match.
Fold it in half along its width. The halves match again.
A diagonal fold does not match, so it has exactly two lines of symmetry.

why.en: Diagonals are not lines of symmetry for a rectangle.

prompt.en: A friend says a rectangle has four lines of symmetry, like a square. How will you explain?

requiredIdeas.en: A square has two extra lines along its diagonals.
In a rectangle that is not a square, folding along a diagonal does not make the halves match.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking every four-sided shape has four lines of symmetry.

points.en: A line of symmetry splits a shape into two matching halves.
A square has four lines, a rectangle two, an equilateral triangle three.
A circle has many lines of symmetry.
